title: Bit manipulation
summary: Bit manipulation treats a number as a row of 0s and 1s. A few operators (AND, OR, XOR and shifts) test, set, clear and combine bits in one step, and a whole set of small items fits in one integer mask.
idea: x & (1 << i) tests bit i; x | (1 << i) sets it; x & (x − 1) clears the lowest 1; a ^ a = 0, so XOR cancels pairs. Masks from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1 list every subset.

signals.see: Every value appears twice except one (or two), and you need O(1) extra space.
signals.think: XOR everything: pairs cancel because a ^ a = 0, and what is left is the lone value.

signals.see: Count 1 bits, check a power of two, or find a missing number in 0..n.
signals.think: x & (x − 1) drops the lowest 1 bit; a power of two has exactly one. XOR of 0..n with the array leaves the missing value.

signals.see: n is small (≤ 20) and you need every subset, or a set of visited items as DP state.
signals.think: Use an integer mask: bit i means item i is in the set. Loop masks from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1.

phrasings: Every number appears twice except one. Find it without extra memory.
For each number from 0 to n, count its 1 bits.
Find the largest XOR of any two numbers in the list.

picture.title: Checking every bit versus clearing the lowest 1
picture.alt: On the left, every one of the 32 bit positions is tested in turn, whether it is 0 or 1. On the right, x & (x − 1) removes the lowest 1 bit at each step, so the loop runs once per 1 bit and stops when x is 0.
picture.caption: x − 1 flips the lowest 1 and the 0s below it; AND keeps the rest.

visualiser.inputHelp: A whole number from 0 to 63, shown as 6 bits.

oneLiner: test x>>i&1; set x|1<<i; clear lowest x&(x-1); XOR cancels pairs; masks 0..2ⁿ-1 are subsets

exercise.prompt: Return every subset of nums, using a bitmask. Mask m includes nums[i] when bit i of m is 1. List the subsets in mask order, 0 to 2ⁿ − 1, keeping each subset in the original order of nums. The starter stops the masks too early.
hints: There are 2ⁿ subsets, one for each mask from 0 to (1 << n) − 1.
Bit i of mask is (mask >> i) & 1. When it is 1, nums[i] is in the subset.
Mask 0 is the empty subset, so an empty nums gives one subset: [].

complexity.why: Each x & (x − 1) step removes one 1 bit, so the loop runs once per 1 bit, at most the word size. Single bit operations are O(1); listing every subset is O(2ⁿ × n).

mistakes: Getting precedence wrong: in JS, x & 1 === 1 parses as x & (1 === 1). Add brackets around bit operations.
Forgetting that JS bit operators work on 32-bit signed integers, so 1 << 31 is negative.
Right-shifting a negative number and expecting the loop to end; use >>> in JS or mask the value.
Using bitmask subsets when n is large: 2ⁿ grows past what any loop can handle.

quiz.question: What does x & (x − 1) do?
choices: Clears the lowest 1 bit of x
quiz.explain: x − 1 flips the lowest 1 and every 0 below it, so AND keeps only the higher bits.

quiz.question: Every value appears twice except one. Why does XOR of all values find it?
choices: a ^ a = 0 and a ^ 0 = a, and XOR order does not matter, so pairs cancel
quiz.explain: XOR is its own inverse and commutative, so the pairs vanish in any order.

quiz.question: How do you check that x > 0 is a power of two?
quiz.explain: A power of two has exactly one 1 bit; clearing it leaves 0.

interviewTip: Write the binary of a small example next to your code and show each operation on it. Bit tricks are much easier to follow on paper than in words.
